//: AI playing styles (nicknames, never real players). short is the scoreboard name in doubles; level is added to the match's AI level; the rest scale the AI's choices: net (how readily its pair takes the net), lob, drop (drop shots and chiquitas), smash (smash rather than bandeja), vibora (víbora rather than bandeja), margin (how far it keeps from lines and walls; lower is riskier), pace (drives, slices, lobs and mid-height volleys: above 0 that share x0.5 hit hard, and drives chosen over slices more; below 0 the reverse with power, below 0 played safe with precision; 0 neither). The sim's default is the neutral 'reloj'; the game deals styles from the seed. El Contragolpe (the M5 roster's counter-puncher, 9 Nov) waits at the back like El Muro but answers with drives rather than lobs (pace a little above 0, fewer lobs and drops) and keeps El Muro's margin: defence turned into attack from the glass. Measured over 100 matches at level 1 (9 Nov): drives 18% of its shots (Relojero 11%, Muro 6%, Martillo 22%), lobs 16% (Muro 31%), at the net 35% of the time (Muro 33%, Relojero 44%), errors 8.7% of shots, between El Muro's 8.1% and Martillo's 10.7% (harder drives from the back hit fewer of their marks than lobs).
